text.p: Byron Black's confidence is rising like the warm weather in the desert.
Black outlasted unseeded Australian Sandon Stolle 6-4 5-7 7-5 on Wednesday to reach the quarterfinals of the $328,000 Arizona tennis tournament.
But after surprising top-seed Marcelo Rios of Chile in a third-set nailbiter on Tuesday, Black found himself in a similar situation -- down a late break to the hard-serving Australian.
But the aggresive double-fisted baseliner had the answer.

"It was very similar match, and today I kept it together," said Black of the two-hour-11-minute victory. "I didn't panic and all because I knew I could break back. I just had the edge on him at the end."
Black lost serve to fall behind 3-5. But he broke Stolle twice and served a pair of aces in the final game to cap a four-game match-ending run for the win.

"I had nothing to lose and I think Sandy put a bit of pressure on himself," said Black, who has one singles title and 14 doubles' crowns since joining the ATP Tour in l991. "I just tried to take it to him. I really tried to be aggressive in that game."
Black knew he would have his hands full against Stolle, who was a semifinalist here last year.

"I knew today it would be tough because Sandy is very dangerous," Black explained. "He's a big player with a big game (12 aces). His serve is tough, he covers the net so well and it's tough to lob because the ball flies due to the altitude."
Black began the new year slowly, hampered by a quadricep injury. But he's in his third quarterfinal and second in as many weeks before losing to Australian Patrick Rafter in Philadelphia last week.
"I really started off the first month struggling a bit and couldn't really get going. Just of late, I've been winning a few matches in succession and that's given me a bit of confidence."
With the rash of upsets, Black has a chance to capture his second singles title though he's not thinking too far ahead just yet.
"I'll play one match at a time," he said. "One at a time."
